[Campaign] [Draft] "Unearthed Arcana: Light, Dark, & Underdark" Has Been Released

Few things I thought of while reading this:

Combine the Deepstalker Ranger with Hunter's Mark (+1d6 damage every time you hit them, takes a bonus action, cannot fail, can be recast for free on a new target if the previous target dies, and you pretty much always know where the mark is).
At level 3, you're looking at 2d8+2d6+ 2 x mod (roughly 24 damage) on the first turn. At level 5, this is now 3d8+3d6+ 3 x improved mod (or 39 damage average). Boom. Headshot.

The Hound of Ill Omen is a Dire Wolf. Most notable things about the Dire Wolf revolve around its massive speed (50) and knocking enemies prone through attacks. Considering enemies adjacent to your Dire Wolf get disadvantage against saving throws, but being knocked prone causes ranged attacks to have disadvantage, it's best to stack spells that rely on saving throws and are not considered "ranged attacks". Frostbite (cantrip, Unearthed Arcana: Elemental Evil), Hold Person (level 2), Blindness/Deafness (level 2), and ESPECIALLY Phantasmal Force (level 2) all come to mind as very effective options. These are also effective in places that use cover, since saving throws ignore cover. Your wolf darts ahead to an enemy who's barely visible, makes the target vulnerable, and your sorcerer takes advantage of that and disables the important target while ignoring their cover.

Light warlocks are interesting, because there's no synergy between the additions and anything the default warlock can add. Nothing.
This isn't a bad thing, since the Undying Light benefits are already good with just the things it gives you, but don't expect there to be many amazing combos you can pull off from the spells you pick or the pact you choose. You don't need extra cantrips (since you have both Light and Sacred Flame) or many rituals, so the book isn't very useful. The Blade eventually deals Necrotic damage, and is only useful for Radiant Resilience. Also, you can't get Flame Blade (which would be AWESOME). There aren't any radiant/fire touch spells that I'm aware of, so you don't really need a familiar. Like I said, this isn't a bad thing, it just makes all three equally viable for this type of Warlock.

A side note, though, a Tiefling would be super strong as a Light Warlock, with its Hellish Rebuke getting the fire damage bonus, Charisma bonus and Darkvision. Kinda awkward that they would get Darkness in a class that's afraid of the dark. Could make for some interesting RP scenarios.

Bitcoin doesn't waste electricity, it's used for security

I don't find this a convincing argument.
Any fiat producing, espionage committing nation state would have no problem gaining over 50% of hashing power, and at that point they can roll back the clock of the bitcoin blockchain.

It's a real issue. Just because it requires a lot of resources doesn't mean that a nation state would have issues accomplishing their goal.

PoS can also be secure without any electrical/computational overhead, and is not really subject to this kind of economic weakness.

I do not think proof of stake as it's described today will provide an alternative consensus mechanism.

The nothing-at-stake problem, where-in miners have no incentive to mine only on the longest chain because the cost associated with mining forks is zero, produces a scenario where consensus on the main chain does not occur. All existing alternatives which a miner sees as viable are asserted as "the real ledger." In Proof of Work, the cost of being wrong creates a disincentive against continuously mining on every fork. Such a strategy of mining all chains would hemorrhage money.

Nothing-at-stake isn't really a problem. Nothing at stake is a voting system where you can vote for all candidates.

The candidate with the most votes still wins (under most PoS rules), it's just a different way to vote.

The consensus rules are what truly dictates, and more importantly what should dictate, what chain is in use.

Authority should come from the chain with "the most power", the the chain that is "the most correct".

By what standard do you determine, presumably for other people, what "should dictate" which chain is used? I make no such assumption on behalf of other people because its not up to me.

There's a fortunate up side to this. You're perfectly free to support a proof of stake design. Even of bitcoin if you want. Your preference is not objective.
